$comment: Worked example from real survey data, and the paper test for the P2 dimension work. Laudio is T1 Adopt (9/9), Playwright, TypeScript, GitHub Actions nightly + per-commit, 6 respondents, migrated off Cypress. Every field below is declared data — none of it required an engine change. Paths and wiring are marked <> where Phase 0 discovery has not happened yet; the profile gate refuses to lock a profile with placeholders, which is the correct answer until someone confirms them.
$d1: Framework. Playwright, TypeScript — they migrated off Cypress.
$d2: Pattern. This one line is why the harness was unadoptable and now is not. bdd-pom does not select ARCH-BOUNDARY, so no-page-object and base-fixture-import are not in their composed rule set — not waived, not excepted, just not describing an architecture they use. Every Tier 0 and Tier 1 concern still applies, CACHED-AUTH included.
$d3: Topology. Their tree, not the adapter's. Rule scope derives from these, so they must exist on disk before the hooks will build a scanner — which is what makes a typo loud instead of silent.

paths.testRoot: <their Playwright root — e.g. e2e or tests>

$d4: Strategy. Their cached login was objection #4, which was a misreading — CACHED-AUTH is the harness's own mandated pattern, so this declaration agrees with the harness rather than deviating from it.
$ruleOverrides: TRACE is Tier 1 with a ratchet: an existing suite cannot be fully tagged on day one, so it onboards at review and ratchets to block. The reason and the date are required — an unrecorded exception is indistinguishable from a mistake.

TRACE.reason: existing suite predates requirement tagging; tagging as modules are touched
